To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an antibody whose Fab has been engineered to bind to HA with a 2:1 (Fab:HA) stoichiometry has been identified, crystallized, and characterized.
a new neutralizing antibody, with a novel 2:1 antibody Fab:HA stoichimetry, has been characterized and crystallized.
an antibody with an unusual stoichiometry of binding to the influenza virus surface glycoprotein HA has been characterized and crystallized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of influenza vaccine.
the development of novel, highly potent and broadly neutralizing antibodies against influenza virus.
the characterization of a new antibody that binds with a 2:1 antibody:FHA stoichiometry and the crystallization of this complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a neutralizing antibody Fab binds to influenza haemagglutinins with 2:1 and 3:1 stoichiometricities.
the antibody binds to two HA molecules simultaneously.
the 2:1 complex is not a crystal packing artefact, and is not a result of the crystallization conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified an antibody with an unprecedented stoichiometry and we have determined the structure of its complex to a resolution that is sufficient to allow us to understand the molecular details that give rise to this unusual stoichiometry.
the antibody is a neutralizing antibody that binds to HA in a 2:1 complex.
we have identified a new antibody that binds to HA with 2:1 antibody:HA stoichiomety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 2:1 antibody-HA complex can be crystallized and that the structure will likely provide a new insight into antibody recognition of the influenza HA.
a neutralizing antibody can bind to HA with a 2:1 complex stoichiometry and that this stoichiometry is not necessarily a consequence of the HA structure.
antibodies can be raised that bind to HA in a stoichiometry that has not been previously observed.
